Getting started with the OSBPG Register

A short guide for new members to logging in, finding your pigs, recording litters, registering breeding stock and keeping your records up to date.

Oxford Sandy and Black Pig Group · Register site: register.osbpg.org

Recording a litter? Most questions are about the Add Farrowing form. Go straight to the step-by-step guide.

What would you like to do?

  • Log in
  • Find your way around
  • See your pigs and litters
  • Download a family tree
  • Record a new litter
  • Register breeding stock
  • Sell, transfer or update a pig
  • Words you'll see

Log in

  1. Go to register.osbpg.org.
  2. Type your Username and Password into the Welcome box. Click the eye icon if you want to check what you've typed.
  3. Tick Remember Me only on your own computer or phone, never on a shared one.
  4. Click Login.

Forgotten your password? Click Lost your password? under the password box and follow the emailed instructions.

Not a member yet? Use the OSBPG Application link in the top menu to join.

Find your way around

Across the top of every page is the main menu: OSBPG Register (the home page), OSBPG Application, Register Dashboard and My Account. Once you're logged in, a Logout link appears there too.

Everything you'll use day to day sits in the panel of green buttons on the right-hand side of the page.

ButtonUse it to
Your Breeding ProfileSee your details, the pigs you own, your litters and the pigs you've bred. More below.
OSBPG Member DirectoryLook up other members of the group.
OSBPG Register DatabaseSearch the wider register of Oxford Sandy and Black pigs and their lineage.
Add FarrowingTell the register about a new litter. More below.
Add Breeding StockAsk for a pig to be registered as pedigree breeding stock. More below.
Update Pig InfoRecord that a pig has died, or transfer it to a new owner. More below.
View All FarrowingsBrowse recorded litters.
Shared Ancestry ToolCheck how closely related two pigs are before you put them together for breeding.

The purple OSBPG Admin Portal button is for the register team only, so you can ignore it.

See your pigs and litters

Click Your Breeding Profile. This page is your herd at a glance, and it's split into four parts as you scroll down.

Your info

Your name, your herd prefix and your address. Your prefix is the herd name that goes at the start of every pig you breed, so it's worth checking it's right. If anything here is wrong, email the register team (details at the end of this guide).

Pigs under your ownership (alive)

Every living pig registered to you, with its name, registration number (RegNo) and ear tag (TAG ID).

  • Click the round + beside a pig to open up its full details.
  • If you have more than ten pigs, use Next and the page numbers at the bottom, or change Show 10 entries to see more at once.

Your farrowings

Every litter you've recorded, each with a Farrowing ID starting OSBF, the date, and how many boars and gilts were born. Click a column heading to sort by it, for example by date.

The buttons underneath let you download certificates for your litters: Farrowing, Weaner and Pork certificates.

Pigs bred by you

Every registered pig that came from your herd, with its date of birth.

Download a family tree

  1. On Your Breeding Profile, click Download Your Pig Family Tree Certificates (under the Pigs Under Your Ownership table).
  2. On the Bloodline & Lineage Generator page, choose one of your pigs from the list.
  3. Save or print the lineage report that's produced.

The report shows three generations: parents, grandparents and great-grandparents, each with their registration number. It's handy to give to a buyer or keep with your herd records.

Record a new litter

Use Add Farrowing to tell the register about each new litter. The litter needs to be on the register before you can register any of its piglets as breeding stock, so it's worth doing soon after the birth.

Before you start, have these to hand

  • The date the litter was born.
  • The name of the sow (the dam) and the boar (the sire). If the boar isn't yours, note his name, RegNo and owner.
  • How many piglets were born in total, including any born dead.
  • For each piglet: male or female, alive or dead, and its tag number if you've tagged it (use a hyphen if not).

Step by step

  1. Log in and click Add Farrowing in the green button panel. Your name and email are filled in for you; check they're correct, as your confirmation email goes to that address.
  2. Enter the Date of Farrowing. Click the small calendar icon and pick the day, rather than typing it, so the day and month can't get mixed up.
  3. Select the Dam from the list. It only shows sows that are registered to you.
  4. Select the Sire from the list. If he isn't there, choose Boar not listed at this step and give his details in Additional Comments at the end.
  5. Under How many piglets were born?, choose the total number born, alive and dead. One row appears for each piglet.
  6. On each piglet row, choose Male or Female, then Alive or Dead.
  7. If a piglet is tagged, type only its own tag number in the small box at the end of its row, for example 44. If it isn't tagged yet, type a single hyphen (-). The box can't be left empty, and a hyphen makes it clear there's no tag yet.
  8. In Additional Comments, add anything the register team should know: details of an unlisted boar, stillbirths, or that the piglets aren't tagged yet.
  9. Check every row, then click Submit. You'll get a confirmation email.

The most common mistake is the tag number. Your herd's tag prefix (the code shown under OSBPG Tag ID, such as WCA04) is added automatically. Type 44, not WCA04-44 or WCA04 44.

If something isn't working

My sow isn't in the Dam list
The list only shows living sows registered to you. Check she appears under Pigs Under Your Ownership on Your Breeding Profile. If you bought her and she's not there, the seller needs to transfer her to you using Update Pig Info; or email the register team.
The boar isn't in the Sire list
Choose Boar not listed and put his name, RegNo (if he has one) and owner in Additional Comments.
Should I include piglets that died?
Yes. Count every piglet born and mark the ones that died as Dead, as in the example above.
I haven't tagged the piglets yet
Type a single hyphen (-) in each tag box and say so in Additional Comments. Please use a hyphen rather than 0, which could be mistaken for a tag number. Don't wait for tagging before recording the litter.
No confirmation email arrived
Check your spam or junk folder. If it isn't there, email the register team before submitting again, so the litter isn't recorded twice.
I made a mistake after submitting
Don't submit the litter again. Email the register team with the date of farrowing, the dam's name, and what needs correcting.
Where can I see the litter now?
It appears under Your Farrowings on Your Breeding Profile with its own Farrowing ID (starting OSBF). You'll use that ID when you register any of its piglets as breeding stock.

Register breeding stock

Use this when you want a pig recorded as a pedigree breeding animal. It sends a request to the register team, who will review it.

  1. Click Add Breeding Stock. Check your name and email.
  2. Answer Is this pig from one of your registered farrowings? If you choose Yes, pick its litter from the Farrowing ID list (each one shows its farrowing date, to help you find it).
  3. Choose the Sex of the pig.
  4. Under OSBPGID Tag, your tag prefix is already filled in. Type the pig's own tag number in the second box (for example 65).
  5. In Additional Comments, describe the pig: its teat count and markings, such as blaze, socks and tail tip.
  6. Click Submit.

Sell, transfer or update a pig

Keep the register accurate whenever a pig leaves your herd or dies.

  1. Click Update Pig Info. Check your name and email.
  2. Select your Pig from the list of pigs registered to you.
  3. Under What do you want to update?, choose one of:
    • a change of status, for example if the pig has died
    • Transfer Ownership to OSBPG Member, if you've sold it to another member
    • a transfer to a non-member
  4. Fill in the extra boxes that appear. For a transfer to a member, choose them from Select member to transfer to; members are listed by herd prefix and name.
  5. Click Submit. You'll get a confirmation email.

Words you'll see

Farrowing
A sow giving birth; also used for the litter itself.
Dam
The mother.
Sire
The father.
Boar
A male pig.
Gilt
A young female pig that hasn't had a litter yet.
Weaner
A young pig that's been weaned from its mother.
Prefix
Your herd name, which goes at the start of every pig you breed (for example Preselihills Clare).
RegNo
A pig's registration number, starting OSBPG.
TAG ID
The pig's ear tag: your herd's tag prefix plus the pig's own number.
Farrowing ID
The register's reference for a litter, starting OSBF.

Need help?

Email the register team at osbreg@oxfordsandyblackpiggroup.org. It helps if you include the pig's name or RegNo, or the Farrowing ID, and say which page you were on.
